current_game_model: Fixed arena with finite wave budget remains the active model.
Level 1 config is rect arena, maxAliveOnions 1, totalOnions 3, spawnIntervalMs 2200, bulletBounces 3.
LevelManager separates active pressure cap, finite budget, queued replacements, and completion condition.
ArenaGates resolves one gate per long arena wall and LevelManager uses resolveGateSpawn before constraining onions into arena.
HUD reads from getWaveProgress(), score state, player boost ratio, and Speed Dot status; it does not own gameplay state.
Normal wave completion path uses resetGame(nextLevel,false,{playerStartPosition}), level-up SFX, level toast, and HUD update rather than blocking level overlay.
design_analysis: Initial presentation passes the first-frame readability smell test on desktop: gates are visible, the current onion is near the top gate, two queued previews are visible outside top/right gate lanes, and the sidebar hierarchy makes LV, OPINION, NEXT WAVE, BOLT, and ONION PRESSURE readable.

Initial presentation passes with notes on mobile: HUD is readable and queue/gates are visible, but the HUD consumes a large top band and the live playfield is comparatively low; this is a readability risk under motion, not an observed failure in static smoke.
The outside-arena terrain/asphalt reads as ground/road rather than galaxy/space in the observed screenshots.
The queue language currently appears coherent at level start: HUD QUEUE shows 2 and two queued onion markers are visible outside gates.
Gate language is visually strong enough to support spawn comprehension, but first-time player comprehension before replacement spawn remains unproven without a human playthrough.
No design justification exists in this pass for new assets, new HUD sections, new mechanics, scoring changes, wave tuning, OnionAI changes, or refactor.
